data.name: Gibraltar
data.region: Southern Europe (Iberian peninsula), British Overseas Territory, outside the EU
data.summary: No capital gains tax (except, from 2025, property dealing by owners of five or more taxable properties), no tax on interest, no inheritance, estate, gift or wealth tax. Dividends are taxable only to the extent the paying company's underlying income is taxable in Gibraltar, so a portfolio of foreign shares produces essentially no Gibraltar tax for a resident. Income tax (up to 39% / 28%) bites mainly on Gibraltar-source and employment income. Category 2 (high-net-worth) status caps assessable income at GBP 118,000 with a GBP 37,000 minimum tax; from June 2026 new applicants need GBP 5 million net assets (was GBP 2 million).

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.description: Income tax on income accruing in or derived from Gibraltar, plus certain foreign income for ordinarily resident individuals; two systems (Allowances Based: top rate 39%; Gross Income Based: top rate 25-28%), taxpayer pays the lower. No tax on capital gains or interest.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if present 183 days in a tax year, or more than 300 days in aggregate over three consecutive tax years. Requires a Gibraltar residence permit or Category 2 certificate.

capital_gains.summary: No tax on capital gains. Exception from 1 Jan 2025: profits on selling Gibraltar property (and shares in property-holding entities) are taxable if the person holds, directly or indirectly, five or more taxable properties (or did so over five consecutive periods); primary residence and estate disposals excluded.
open_questions: Statute (Income Tax Act 2010 as amended for property gains from 2025) not opened.
capital_gains.rate_basis: No CGT. real_estate_local 0 assumes fewer than five taxable Gibraltar properties.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading as a business (in Gibraltar) could be taxable trading income; not researched.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxable only to the extent the company's underlying income is taxable in Gibraltar. Dividends from foreign companies with no Gibraltar-taxable income are therefore effectively untaxed (implied by PwC, not stated directly). No tax on interest.

sources.title: Gibraltar - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Treatment of foreign dividends received by an ordinarily resident individual is implied, not stated, by PwC; the 'certain income received in other places' rule for ordinarily residents is not described.
dividends.rate_basis: Foreign portfolio dividends: underlying income not taxable in Gibraltar, so 0. Gibraltar company dividends: taxed at personal rates (up to 39%) to the extent of taxable underlying profits, with credit for company tax (not verified), so domestic_rate left null.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends (general knowledge, not verified).
dividends.treaty_network: Essentially no comprehensive double tax treaties (UK-Gibraltar treaty signed 2019 only); full non-treaty WHT on foreign dividends (not verified).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: General rates (municipal property rates) apply; not researched.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax, no estate duty and no gift tax. Stamp duty applies to transfers of Gibraltar real estate and shares in companies owning it (up to 4.5% on the excess over GBP 800,000), mainly on sales.
open_questions: Whether stamp duty applies to an inheritance or gift of Gibraltar property to a child not confirmed.

regimes.name: Category 2 high-net-worth individual
regimes.description: Assessable income capped at GBP 118,000 a year, taxed only under the Allowances Based System; minimum tax GBP 37,000 and maximum tax GBP 42,380 a year at current rates (Income Tax Office Q&A). Mainly useful for individuals with large Gibraltar-taxable income; for a passive foreign portfolio (no CGT, foreign dividends and interest effectively untaxed) it chiefly provides a residence route and certainty, at the cost of the minimum tax.
regimes.eligibility: Not resident in Gibraltar in the previous 5 years; net assets of at least GBP 5 million (GBP 2 million for applications before June 2026); approved residential accommodation for exclusive use.
regimes.duration_note: No time limit: Category 2 status lasts for as long as the individual holds the Category 2 certificate issued by Gibraltar Finance and keeps meeting its conditions (approved residential accommodation, net assets); the Income Tax Office Q&A gives no expiry.

lump_sum.notes: Minimum tax GBP 37,000; maximum GBP 42,380 a year at current rates, because assessable income is capped at GBP 118,000 (Income Tax Office Q&A, read 2026-10-15). PwC's example (GBP 42,380 'on income of GBP 105,000') reflects an older cap. Coverage of a spouse/children under one certificate not verified.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent of 13 residential lettings with 4+ bedrooms on PropertyGibraltar.com on 2026-10-15 (14 listed; one at GBP 895, evidently a room let, excluded). Range GBP 3,350-14,000; South District and Westside villas GBP 6,700-14,000. Large family houses are scarce; most are apartments. Asking rents in GBP (GIP at par). Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

succession.name: Gibraltar
succession.summary: Gibraltar has no forced heirship and applies English-style rules. Trusts are fully recognised and the Hague Trusts Convention was extended to Gibraltar. Private foundations are available under a 2017 law.
succession.family_claims: Gibraltar has an English-style family provision claim; the statute was not identified.
succession.foreign_law_note: Movables follow the law of the deceased's domicile, immovables follow Gibraltar law. There is no choice of nationality law.
succession.trust_note: Hague Convention extended to Gibraltar (1 January 1992 per a Dutch treaty record). Foundations are governed by the Gibraltar private foundations law of 2017; its exact title was not verified.
open_questions: The HCCH status-table page could be read only in an older cached version that does not show territorial extensions; extension dates come from the UK Treaty Series 14 (1992) and a Dutch treaty record, and should be re-checked on hcch.net.
